    "text": "Engineering Handbook - Meridian Financial Services. Architecture Overview. This document describes the overall system architecture for the MFS platform, including payment processing, fraud detection, and customer-facing services. Service Architecture. The MFS platform is built on a microservices architecture deployed to OpenShift Container Platform (OCP). Core services include mfs-payment-gateway (deployed on mfs-pay-pod-01 in namespace mfs-payments), mfs-fraud-engine (deployed on mfs-fraud-pod-01 in namespace mfs-fraud), mfs-customer-portal (deployed on mfs-portal-pod-01 in namespace mfs-portal), and shared libraries in mfs-common-libs. All services communicate via REST APIs through the API gateway at api-gateway.mfs.internal and asynchronous event streaming through Kafka at kafka-broker.mfs.internal. Service accou

ST APIs through the API gateway at api-gateway.mfs.internal and asynchronous event streaming through Kafka at kafka-broker.mfs.internal. Service accounts follow the naming convention svc-<service-name> with least-privilege access. Infrastructure Layout. Production databases are hosted on dedicated PostgreSQL instances: pghost-prod-01.mfs.internal (mfs_payments_db), pghost-prod-02.mfs.internal (mfs_fraud_db), pghost-prod-03.mfs.internal (mfs_audit_db), and pghost-prod-04.mfs.internal (mfs_customers_db). Redis caching is provided by redis-cluster.mfs.internal. HSM integration for card tokenization connects to hsm-gateway.mfs.internal on port 8443. The production cluster is ocp-prod-east.mfs.internal running OpenShift 4.14. Secrets management is handled by HashiCorp Vault at vault.mfs.internal. Team Structure. The platform is maintained by three engineering squads: Payments Core (lead: Arjun Deshmukh, 6 engineers), Fraud and Risk (lead: Priya Natarajan, 5 engineers), and Platform Engineering (lead: Marcus Thompson, 4 engineers). The Director of Engineering is Samantha Rodriguez. Architecture decisions are reviewed by the Architecture Review Board chaired by David Kim (VP Engineering).

    "text": "Payment Gateway Operational Runbook. Last updated: 2026-09-28 by Arjun Deshmukh. Service Overview. The mfs-payment-gateway service processes all payment transactions for Meridian Financial Services. It runs on mfs-pay-pod-01 in the mfs-payments namespace on ocp-prod-east.mfs.internal. The service connects to mfs_payments_db on pghost-prod-01.mfs.internal using service account svc-payment-api. It publishes transaction events to the txn-events Kafka topic on kafka-broker.mfs.internal. The service also connects to the HSM gateway at hsm-gateway.mfs.internal:8443 for card tokenization and encryption operations. Redis caching at redis-cluster.mfs.internal is used for idempotency keys and rate limiting. Health Checks. The /health endpoint returns service status. Check database connectivity: verify pghost-prod-01.mfs.internal is reachable on port 5432. Check Redis connectivity: verify redis-cluster.mfs.internal is reachable on port 6379. Check Kafka producer health: verify kafk

eachable on port 5432. Check Redis connectivity: verify redis-cluster.mfs.internal is reachable on port 6379. Check Kafka producer health: verify kafka-broker.mfs.internal is reachable on port 9092. Check HSM gateway: verify hsm-gateway.mfs.internal is reachable on port 8443. Monitor the Grafana dashboard at grafana.mfs.internal/d/payment-gateway-slo for SLO metrics. Incident Response Procedures. Step 1: Acknowledge the PagerDuty alert from payments-oncall schedule. Step 2: Check the Grafana dashboard for payment-gateway SLOs. Step 3: Inspect logs in Kibana at kibana.mfs.internal using query service:mfs-payment-gateway AND level:ERROR. Step 4: Check recent deployments via the deployment timeline in Datadog. Step 5: If database related, check pghost-prod-01.mfs.internal connection pool metrics. Step 6: If tokenization related, verify HSM gateway status. Step 7: Escalate to Arjun Deshmukh if not resolved within 15 minutes. Deployment Procedures. Deployments use GitLab CI/CD pipeline. Production deployments require approval from the payments-oncall lead and a successful staging deployment. Canary deployments roll out to 10% of traffic first. Full rollout requires manual approval after

ents-oncall lead and a successful staging deployment. Canary deployments roll out to 10% of traffic first. Full rollout requires manual approval after 30-minute canary window. Rollback Procedures. Execute rollback via GitLab CI/CD: trigger the rollback-production job in the latest pipeline. Alternatively, use oc rollback on ocp-prod-east.mfs.internal to revert the mfs-pay-pod-01 deployment. Kafka producer errors: Check kafka-broker.mfs.internal broker health and txn-events topic partition status. Redis connection errors: Check redis-cluster.mfs.internal cluster node health.     "text": "Fraud Detection System Documentation. Last updated: 2026-09-25 by Priya Natarajan. System Architecture. The mfs-fraud-engine is the core fraud detection service for Meridian Financial Services. It runs on mfs-fraud-pod-01 in the mfs-fraud namespace on ocp-prod-east.mfs.internal. The service uses an ensemble approach combining ML model predictions (XGBoost) with rule-based scoring from the AML engine. Transaction events are consumed from the txn-events Kafka topic on

bining ML model predictions (XGBoost) with rule-based scoring from the AML engine. Transaction events are consumed from the txn-events Kafka topic on kafka-broker.mfs.internal by the KafkaConsumer in features/stream.py. Fraud scores are published to the fraud-scores topic, and AML alerts are published to the aml-alerts topic. The database mfs_fraud_db on pghost-prod-02.mfs.internal stores historical fraud scores, velocity windows, AML alerts, and model metadata. Service account: svc-fraud-engine. Model Training Pipeline. Models are trained on a weekly cadence using historical transaction data from mfs_fraud_db. The training pipeline uses scikit-learn for feature preprocessing and XGBoost for the gradient-boosted tree model. Training data includes velocity features, amount patterns, geographic risk scores, and merchant category codes. Model artifacts are stored in the MLflow registry at mlflow.mfs.internal:5000. Model promotion from staging to production requires approval from Priya Natarajan and a minimum F1 score of 0.94 on the holdout test set. Feature Engineering. The FeatureExtractor class in features/extractor.py computes three main feature groups: velocity features (transacti

ut test set. Feature Engineering. The FeatureExtractor class in features/extractor.py computes three main feature groups: velocity features (transaction frequency over sliding windows), amount pattern features (statistical distribution of transaction amounts), and geographic risk features (IP geolocation, shipping-billing address mismatch). Feature vectors are computed in real-time from Redis-backed sliding windows managed by the VelocityMonitor. AML Rule Engine. The AMLRuleEngine in rules/aml_engine.py implements regulatory compliance rules for anti-money laundering. Key rules include structuring detection (multiple transactions just below reporting thresholds), rapid movement patterns, and geographic risk flagging. Suspicious activities are flagged with severity levels and stored in the mfs_fraud_db aml_alerts table. The rule engine publishes flagged transactions to the aml-alerts Kafka topic for compliance team review. Velocity Monitoring. The VelocityMonitor in engine/velocity.py maintains sliding windows in Redis at redis-cluster.mfs.internal for transaction velocity tracking. Windows are configurable at 1-minute, 5-minute, 1-hour, and 24-hour intervals. Thresholds are dynamic

.mfs.internal for transaction velocity tracking. Windows are configurable at 1-minute, 5-minute, 1-hour, and 24-hour intervals. Thresholds are dynamically adjusted based on merchant category and historical baselines. Model Serving and Versioning. The ModelServing class in serving/server.py provides a FastAPI-based inference endpoint. Models are loaded from the MLflow registry. The service supports A/B testing between model versions. Total estimated rows: 24M across all tables. PII fields are encrypted using EncryptionUtil from mfs-common-libs. Schema version: v2026.08.10. mfs_audit_db. Host: pghost-prod-03.mfs.internal, por

    "text": "API Gateway Configuration. The API gateway at api-gateway.mfs.internal routes external and internal API traffic to backend services. It runs on the mfs-platform namespace on ocp-prod-east.mfs.internal. Routing Rules. /payments/v2/* -> mfs-payment-gateway (mfs-pay-pod-01, namespace mfs-payments, port 8080). /fraud/v2/* -> mfs-fraud-engine (mfs-fraud-pod-01, namespace mfs-fraud, port 8080). /tokens/v1/* -> mfs-payment-gateway (mfs-pay-pod-01, tokenization endpoints, port 8080). /settlements/v1/* -> mfs-payment-gateway (mfs-pay-pod-01, settlement endpoints, port 8080). /aml/v1/* -> mfs-fraud-engine (mfs-fraud-pod-01, AML endpoints, port 8080). Rate Limiting. Global rate limit: 10,000 requests per minute per API key. Per-endpoint limits: POST /pa

(mfs-fraud-pod-01, AML endpoints, port 8080). Rate Limiting. Global rate limit: 10,000 requests per minute per API key. Per-endpoint limits: POST /payments/v2/payments: 1,000 rpm. GET /payments/v2/payments: 5,000 rpm. POST /fraud/v2/score: 2,000 rpm. Rate limit headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset. Rate limit state stored in redis-cluster.mfs.internal. Authentication. All external API calls require OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens. Internal service-to-service calls use mTLS with service account certificates from vault.mfs.internal. API keys are managed through the API portal at api.mfs.internal. Token validation is performed by the AuthClient from mfs-common-libs. CORS Configuration. Allowed origins: https://portal.mfs.internal, https://admin.mfs.internal. Allowed methods: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS. Allowed headers: Authorization, Content-Type, X-Request-ID. Max age: 86400 seconds. TLS Configuration. TLS 1.3 only. Certificate provider: vault.mfs.internal PKI engine. Certificate rotation: automatic, 30-day rotation. Cipher suites: TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256.",
